summary: Round 3, narrow. Measured against the STAGED bytes in an isolated copy (git show :scripts/check-fault-store-records.sh into a scratch dir with lib.sh beside it and the real sequencer/ symlinked), because the working tree was moving under me mid-review. (1) THE EXIT-STATUS FIX WORKS: with a python3 stub exiting 127 the gate prints FAIL 'the predicate did not run -- python3 exited non-zero', exit 1; with a stub that prints 'EXAMINED 12' and THEN exits 1 it still fails, so a partial write before a crash does not read as a clean count. My round-2 minor is closed on measurement, not on the claim. (2) THE COUNT-FROM-PREDICATE CHANGE BROKE NOTHING I PASSED AT ROUND 2: deleting each of the twelve record(...) lines in FaultInjectingStore.java in turn still refuses 12 of 12 under the staged script, with the right line number and the right verb named; no-verbs still exits 1 with 'lost its subject'; one-branch-only and commented-out still refuse; two-unmetered still names both. EXAMINED is the loop's own counter and agrees with the store's twelve @Override lines. (3) THE FOUR MUTATIONS THE TEST ROLE FOUND ARE ALL KILLED, re-measured by me: examine-only-the-first (3 assertions red), skip-past-line-100 (realStore red), double-the-count (24 vs 12, red), default-repointed-at-a-fixture (2 vs 12, red). missing[:1] is killed by two-unmetered; dropping the zero-verb guard is killed by no-verbs; is_comment->False is killed by no-verbs. No production code, no object-store request path, nothing that scales with records, shards, partitions or indices -- the only runtime effect is one more pre-commit script. Two minors below, both surviving mutations I measured, both about what the suite does NOT pin rather than about the gate being wrong. Neither blocks; recording them rather than asking for a round 4.

findings.title: the exit-status guard that fixes my round-2 minor is itself unpinned -- deleting it leaves the whole suite green
findings.failure_scenario: The `|| { fail "the predicate did not run ..."; finish; }` block appended to the command substitution is the fix for round 2's minor, and it does fire (measured above). But nothing in FaultStoreRecordsTest constructs a crashing predicate, so the guard is not constrained by any test. Measured: I removed the block cleanly from the staged script (leaving `RAW=$(python3 ... PY)` with no status check) and re-ran a faithful reimplementation of all eleven assertions of FaultStoreRecordsTest -- 10 of 10 green, zero red. The concrete failure is the same one the fix closed, one refactor later: someone tidying the heredoc, switching to `scripts/fault_store_scan.py` to match the siblings, or wrapping the call in a function drops the guard, the suite stays green, check-harness-tests stays green, and the gate silently returns to printing `ok 12 verb(s) metered` on any file whose parse raises. Pinning it costs one T0 case -- put a `python3` stub that exits non-zero first on PATH via ProcessBuilder.environment(), assert exit 1 and 'the predicate did not run'. Minor and not blocking because the guard is present and correct in the staged bytes; it is regression cover that is missing, not the fix.

findings.title: `stmt.startswith('record(')` weakened to `'record(' in stmt` survives every fixture -- a one-line guarded call meters one branch and passes
findings.failure_scenario: The eight fixtures pin 'first statement' against a MULTI-LINE early return (metered-on-one-branch-only puts `if (k == null) {` first) and against a comment, but none puts a guarded call on ONE line. Measured: with `elif 'record(' not in stmt:` substituted for the staged `elif not stmt.startswith('record('):`, all 10 reimplemented assertions stay green. The shape that then passes is `@Override public String stat(String k) { \n    if (faults.countRefusals()) record("stat");` -- the staged script refuses it (verified, exit 1, 'first statement is: if (faults.countRefusals()) record("stat");'), the mutant accepts it with `ok 1 verb(s) metered`. That is exactly metered-on-one-branch-only's defect written one line shorter, and it is the shape a verb author most plausibly writes when they want the call above `refuseIfPartitioned()` but only on the counted path. A ninth fixture with the guard inlined closes it. Minor because the staged predicate is the strict one and behaves correctly; what is missing is a fixture that would notice if it stopped being.

findings.title: process: the WORKING TREE of the file under review currently carries an unstaged mutation of this line, and that mutation survives the entire suite
findings.failure_scenario: `git status` reports `AM scripts/check-fault-store-records.sh`: the index holds blob 4868039 (the reviewed bytes, diff sha 4897854d...) while the working tree has line 89's comment skip reduced from `if not t or t.startswith('//') or t.startswith('/*') or t.startswith('*'):` to `if not t:`. The commit itself is safe -- git commits the index and pre-commit stashes unstaged changes -- but two things follow. First, that mutation SURVIVES all 10 reimplemented assertions, so the suite would not notice it either way: measured against a copy of the real store with `// count the refused call too -- ADR-0010` inserted above `record("stat")`, the staged script says `ok 12 verb(s) metered` and the worktree script FAILS with `first statement is: // count the refused call too`. A legal verb shape -- a comment explaining why the call sits where it does, which is the one thing this gate's own header spends thirty lines doing -- becomes a false refusal, and no test says so. Second, if the mutation is still there at `git add -A` time it lands as unreviewed bytes under a verdict hash that does not cover it. Revert the working tree to the index before committing, and confirm `git status` shows a clean `A ` rather than `AM`.
